title: The Hiking Trip
victoryHeadline: Caught! Turns out the only predator on this trail walked on two legs.
acts: By the time the trailhead sign-in sheet had dried, the group had split into factions nobody had actually organized. On the Windy Trail, Aubrey declared herself keeper of the cap club's one bylaw — matching hats, no exceptions — and spent the walk drafting an amendment to close what she considered Hank's loophole, while Brianna kept a private step count she refused, on principle, to admit she was losing. Hank, drafted into the club against his will and wearing the smallest cap on offer, spent most of the hike observing that it never used to take three people to lose a footpath. Down on the Rocky Trail, Clark and Finlay had both shown up in sunglasses despite the cloud cover and took this as proof they were meant to hike together — Clark filling a pocket notebook with a private rock-classification system, Finlay pleased with himself for finding what he was already calling the shortcut.

The shortcut, as it turned out, ran straight toward the one stretch of woods the printed map quietly asked everyone to avoid, and Finlay got close enough to the real thing to hear something move in the undergrowth before deciding, wisely, that he did not want to know what. He never mentioned it to Clark, or to anyone. Deeper in, at the edge of Bear Woods proper, Joe was pointing out claw marks on a trunk to Vincenza — headphones in, sunglasses on, gamely not listening to a word — and telling her the local bear was far more interested in berries than hikers. Back at the Ranger's Hut, Elias worked steadily down his waiver list, ticking off names as stragglers filtered back in ones and twos, in no particular hurry yet.

By late afternoon the list had one gap left on it, and it stayed a gap. Everyone else was accounted for — cap club and all, Clark's sunglasses finally off, Finlay none the wiser about how close his shortcut had come to costing him a very different afternoon. Vincenza wasn't among the returning stragglers. Joe was, freshly arrived, hands rinsed clean at the stream by the trailhead, with no bear story left to tell and nothing at all to add to the headcount.

whereabouts.A: Aubrey had appointed herself keeper of the Windy Trail cap club's one bylaw — matching hats, mandatory — and spent the walk drafting an amendment to close what she considered a loophole in Hank's favor.
whereabouts.B: Brianna had set herself a private step-count target for the Windy Trail and was refusing, on principle, to admit how far short of it she'd fallen.
whereabouts.C: Clark hadn't taken his sunglasses off since the trailhead, overcast sky or not, and was quietly filling a pocket notebook with a rock-classification system he had no intention of showing anyone.
whereabouts.D: Danika had wanted the Pine Forest to herself since the itinerary was first mentioned, and now that she had it, she sat on a fallen log matching birdsong to a folded card she kept in her cardigan pocket.
whereabouts.E: Elias had the waiver clipboard, a headcount to run, and no particular interest in whether anyone thought that made him the least fun person on the trip.
whereabouts.F: Finlay kept his sunglasses on despite the cloud cover and had drifted further up the Rocky Trail than the printed map really allowed, pleased with himself for finding what he was already calling the shortcut.
whereabouts.G: Gavin had stopped photographing the view an hour ago and switched to cataloguing boulders in a private numbering system nobody at work had ever heard him mention.
whereabouts.H: Hank had been folded into the Windy Trail cap club against his will, wore the smallest cap available on principle, and spent most of the walk announcing that it never used to take three people to find a footpath.
whereabouts.I: Iris had claimed the Booth's one decent chair within four minutes of arriving and fully intended to still be sitting in it when everyone else came back.
whereabouts.J: Joe stood at the edge of Bear Woods pointing out a set of claw marks on a nearby trunk, telling Vincenza the local bear was far more interested in berries than hikers.
whereabouts.K: Kobe had worn the plaid on purpose, hoping the Grove's dappled light would let him get close enough to photograph a woodpecker without spooking it off its branch, and hadn't accounted for how completely the same trick would make him vanish from a distance.
whereabouts.V: Vincenza had her headphones in and her sunglasses on and had tuned out precisely everyone, which was, by her own account, the entire point of the trip.

reveal: It was Joe, in Bear Woods, and there was never a second bear involved at all — only him, a fallen branch, and thirty seconds bought by a story about claw marks. He'd spotted the real bear's tracks earlier that day and borrowed its reputation rather than its company: a rustle he made himself, a warning that sent Vincenza's attention exactly the wrong way, and the branch already in his hand before she'd worked out there was nothing behind her. By the time Elias reached the bottom of his list, Joe had rinsed his hands in the stream and had nothing left to tell anyone.

escape.generic: Somewhere out there, an entirely innocent bear is still getting blamed for something it had nothing to do with, while the person who borrowed its reputation is already back at the trailhead, loading up the car.

byAccused.A: Aubrey's only complaint, the whole way into the ranger's truck, was that nobody had let her finish the amendment.
byAccused.B: Brianna never did admit to the real number, and now, technically, she never has to.
byAccused.C: Clark was marched off still wearing the sunglasses, which he felt was at least consistent, if nothing else.
byAccused.D: Danika's bird-call card sat abandoned on the log for the rest of the afternoon, which was closer to alone than she'd actually wanted.
byAccused.E: The rangers filed Elias's own waiver as evidence against him, which he considered, even under arrest, a serious breach of paperwork etiquette.
byAccused.F: Finlay was hauled off still congratulating himself on the shortcut, never finding out how close it had actually come to a very different kind of story.
byAccused.G: The rest of the group agreed the boulder numbering system made a lot more sense once someone explained it was evidence, not a hobby.
byAccused.H: Hank was hauled off still muttering that it never used to take a search party this large to arrest the wrong hiker either.
byAccused.I: Iris's chair sat empty at the Booth for the rest of the day, which everyone quietly agreed was the real crime.
byAccused.K: Kobe's plaid shirt turned out to be excellent camouflage right up until it wasn't, and he spent the whole walk out insisting the woodpecker would back him up.
